关键词: European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD)
主要内容: The U.S. Department of the Treasury welcomed the IFI Action Plan to Address Food Insecurity, developed by the Asian Development Bank (ADB), the African Development Bank (AfDB), the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD), the International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD), the Inter-American Development Bank (IDB), the International Monetary Fund (IMF), and the World Bank Group. This initiative stems from a meeting convened by Secretary Yellen in April 2022, which included leaders from the IMF, World Bank, IFAD, and Finance Ministers of Indonesia and Germany. The Russian war against Ukraine has intensified global food insecurity, driven by conflict, climate change, and economic downturns. The IFIs are working to address rising food insecurity through financing, policy engagement, technical assistance, and knowledge work. The IFI Action Plan outlines how IFIs are scaling their efforts in food security and agriculture. ADB is working with the World Food Program and FAO to address food insecurity through emergency food assistance, food-for-work, and cash-for-work programs. ADB is financing $200 million in Afghanistan for essential food and livelihood services and exploring trade finance and private sector loans for food imports. AfDB is supporting a $1.5 billion facility to deliver climate-smart seeds, fertilizers, and extension services to 20 million farmers. EBRD’s Resilience and Livelihood Framework will support businesses and public services affected by the war in Ukraine, with €500 million allocated for food security and trade finance. IDB will support social programs targeting food insecure populations, including cash transfers and school meals, with a $60 million program for Haiti. IFAD aims to invest $3.5 billion in 78 countries to address food insecurity. The U.S. Department of the Treasury has welcomed the IFI Action Plan to address food insecurity, emphasizing the need to build resilience among the world’s poorest and most vulnerable rural populations against current global challenges, including the Ukraine crisis and other food system shocks over the next three years. IFAD’s newly launched Crisis Response Initiative aims to address short-term food security needs in 22 countries, primarily in Africa and Asia. IFAD has received initial pledges of €11 million for the initiative. The IMF will support countries affected by food insecurity using its full range of instruments, focusing on macroeconomic expertise. It will work closely with the World Bank and other IFIs to provide policy advice, capacity development assistance, and financial support. The World Bank Group will provide $30 billion in solutions over the next 15 months, with $12 billion for new projects and $18 billion in undisbursed balance. The response will focus on mitigating short-term impacts of food and fertilizer price crises while addressing long-term resilience and food system transformation.
